public_rationale: The behavioral tests show that strong benchmark results can coexist with failures on basic capabilities relevant to the same tasks. That supports the ordinary contextual claim that benchmark success alone does not establish general, reliable intelligence. It does not settle a philosophical definition of intelligence or prove near-universal agreement within the community.
limitations: The assessment depends on reading intelligent as broad, reliable competence in the surrounding AGI discussion.
The evidence concerns language models and does not imply that benchmarks are useless.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Doing well on a benchmark does not amount to being intelligent.

statement.excerpt: The dirty little secret that pretty much everyone in the AI community knows is that doing well on a benchmark is not actually tantamount to being intelligent.
statement.document_title: No, Virginia, AGI is not imminent

our_interpretation: In the AGI discussion, the plain reading is that a high benchmark score alone does not establish broad, reliable cognitive competence.
This does not assert that benchmark performance provides no evidence of ability or that benchmark-tested systems possess no intelligence.
The surrounding 2019-to-2023 discussion supplies the period for the empirical assessment.
The community-awareness language is treated as emphasis; no literal near-unanimity estimate is inferred.
criteria.support_condition: Systems with strong benchmark scores fail basic novel tests of abilities that those scores might reasonably be taken to establish.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes that the benchmark scores in question are sufficient to demonstrate the broad, reliable competence being inferred, including performance on novel tests.
